column3: NKJV has “on the second Sabbath after the first,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has only “on a Sabbath.”
NKJV has “took and ate … and also gave,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “having taken … ate and gave.” “The loaves of the presentation” is rendered “the showbread.”
NKJV has “also,” following the Textus Receptus wording; the critical text reads “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
NKJV has “I will ask you one thing,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “I ask you, is it lawful.”
NKJV includes “as whole as the other,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text ends with “his hand was restored.”
Close to the Greek; “Judas of James” is rendered “Judas the son of James.”
NKJV joins the start of verse 18 (“who came to hear Him and be healed of their diseases”) to this verse.
NKJV begins this verse with “as well as those who were tormented,” having placed “who came to hear Him …” in verse 17.
Close to the Greek; “you are receiving” is rendered “you have received.”
NKJV lacks “now” after “full,” as does the Textus Receptus; the critical text includes it.
Close to the Greek; “mistreat” is rendered “spitefully use.”
